name: Dienolone
lead: Dienolone (also nordienolone, RU-3118, trenazone, dienazone) is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid of the 19-nortestosterone group. It was developed under the code RU-3118 and never marketed.[1]

Based on rat and rabbit tissue bioassays, it has slightly lower affinity than nandrolone for androgen and progesterone receptors; trenbolone has similar androgen receptor affinity but several-fold higher progesterone receptor affinity.[1] Its main practical role in the literature is as a chemical intermediate, including in routes to trenbolone and other steroids.[1]

paras: Wikipedia describes a synthesis from prenortestosterone by bromination and two dehydrohalogenations, and notes 2022 and 2024 patents claiming use as a trenbolone precursor. Methyldienolone and ethyldienolone are orally active 17-alkylated derivatives, and dienedione is its 17-keto analogue, thought to act as a prohormone.[1]

card.summary: A never-marketed nandrolone-like steroid, mainly of interest as a chemical intermediate.
card.note: No human studies; sources are thin.

quick.overview:
Dienolone is a 19-nortestosterone steroid developed under the code RU-3118 and never sold as a drug.

Sources describe its receptor affinities in animal tissue and its role as a synthesis intermediate; no human data exist.
quick.mechanism: It binds androgen and progesterone receptors slightly less strongly than nandrolone in animal tissue assays.
